name: Server4Agent

modes.label: Native product meter; not a general-purpose 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM
modes.note: Not auto-rankable for generic VM workloads. Native price and usage limits are preserved in provider rate_cards/extras and regimes. Empty sizes intentionally prevents inventing CPU/RAM capacity or treating missing rates as zero.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 1 server; small tier; 5 GB/server; 1 public project; 10 GB monthly egress; $2 trial credits.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: 2 small servers; 5 GB/server; 3 public projects; 100 GB egress; 3 members.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: 3 small/medium servers; 20 GB/server; 10 public projects; 250 GB egress; 5 members.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: 10 servers, small/medium/large; 100 GB/server; 30 public projects; 1 TB egress; 15 members.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Unlimited advertised servers, custom storage/credits; managed or BYOC.

caveats: vCPU/RAM of server tiers and base compute meter unpublished.
Plan fee is not wholly credit: Starter $29 includes $10; Pro $99 includes $40; Business $299 includes $150.
Displayed ~1.4x Starter/Pro and ~1.2x Business AI overage are approximate and applied to an unpublished base; cannot derive a unit price.
Default managed-server caps stop at 10, so 50 concurrent servers requires Enterprise contract.
Project count is not sandbox concurrency; no inference that many projects each get a separate 4/8 VM.
Early-access CTA leaves onboarding availability untested; no account created.
Native billing cannot be reduced to a 4-vCPU/8-GiB price. No matching engine sizes, by design.

Included credits reset every billing period (no rollover). Free plan hard-stops; paid plans can allow overage (~1.4x base on Starter/Pro, ~1.2x on Business) or keep a strict cap. Budget caps can be slightly exceeded because of propagation delays.
Product is still early access: every plan CTA is a waitlist button and /waitlist redirects to /?waitlist=1; self-serve signup not confirmed.
Annual billing gives 2 months free: Starter $290/yr (~$24/mo), Pro $990/yr (~$83/mo), Business $2,990/yr (~$249/mo). Not encoded as plans.

Included credits may cover only AI/agent work: a Server4Agent blog says server tiers (small/medium/large) and egress are metered separately and 'priced by capacity' (no tier price published), while the pricing FAQ says a credit is '$1 of metered usage (compute + AI)'. Treat included_usd as applying to AI usage only until clarified.

fleet.tiers: Free 1 server; Starter 2; Pro 3; Business 10; Enterprise advertised unlimited.
fleet.notes: 10 needs Business; 50/300/1,000 need Enterprise. Server-count entitlement includes shape restrictions, not a single interchangeable CPU pool.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Servers scale to zero when idle; state persists on a durable volume mounted at `/home/node/workspace`.
snapshot_auto.note: Idle scale-to-zero keeps the disk (persistent_disk), not a snapshot; nothing says memory/processes are saved. Paused projects 'stop processes and cron until resumed'.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: POST /projects/{id}/export packages the project into one file and returns a time-limited link to it
snapshot_on_demand.note: The full MCP tool list ('MCP tools (complete list)') and the OpenAPI spec have no snapshot/checkpoint/fork endpoint. Project export/import copies the source tree, settings and run plan (no dependency caches, git history or .env) to another server; that is a code bundle, not a machine snapshot.

harness_api.quote: A goal sent to the build agent against a project. Created from the dashboard task composer or via MCP `prompt`. Supports follow-up threads, file attachments (up to 5), optional model tier selection, cancellation, and `awaiting_input` when the agent needs a human answer.
harness_api.note: Provider's own on-server 'build agent' only (no Claude Code/Codex harnesses). MCP `prompt({server_id, prompt})` and REST POST /servers/{id}/tasks ('Give the agent a goal'), GET tasks list/get with status, question, latest progress log; project_id threads a run 'onto that project as a follow-up'; webhooks task.created/completed/failed. No token-level event streaming documented (poll or webhooks).

ingress_rules.quote: Once it is live you choose who may open it: anyone with the link, or only your team.
ingress_rules.note: Per project: visibility private (URL serves nothing) by default vs public; access 'public' or 'team' (sign-in required, can be narrowed to named members). Public apps behind WAF/DDoS protection. No IP allowlists or port selection documented; no raw ports.

secret_proxy.quote: Injected as environment variables at run time
secret_proxy.note: Encrypted vault, per-account/server/project scoping, write-only via API, but values enter the server as env vars. No injecting proxy.
